system.name: FRACTAL
system.one_liner: a system for fault-tolerant distribution of unmodified POSIX shell scripts across executor nodes using exactly-once remote pipes

components.name: PaSh-JIT Compiler
components.role: just-in-time compiler that parses a POSIX shell script into an AST and emits a command-level DFG

components.name: blk1
components.role: one DFG subgraph derived from the client shell script

components.name: blk2
components.role: another DFG subgraph derived from the client shell script

components.name: Main
components.role: subgraph type containing the AST region unsafe for distribution, executed on the client/authoritative node

components.name: Merger
components.role: subgraph type containing an aggregator vertex (e.g., sort -m) that merges outputs of multiple upstream subgraphs

components.name: Regular
components.role: subgraph type without an aggregator vertex

components.name: Remote Pipe
components.role: lightweight primitive replacing a Unix pipe at inter-subgraph edges, recording byte-level progress and enforcing exactly-once semantics

components.name: Coordinator
components.role: groups subgraphs by type (A1), instruments edges with remote pipes (A2), decides persistence (A3), and schedules/monitors executors (A4-6)

components.name: Progress Monitor
components.role: tracks execution progress of scheduled subgraphs

components.name: Executor
components.role: receives assigned subgraphs, reconstructs them into shell scripts, and runs them in a non-blocking event loop

components.name: Executor Runtime
components.role: runs the reconstructed shell script for an assigned subgraph

components.name: Event Queue
components.role: queues events for the executor's non-blocking event loop

components.name: Event loop
components.role: tight, non-blocking loop maximizing CPU utilization without oversubscription

components.name: DFS File Reader
components.role: reads input data for the subgraph from the distributed file system

components.name: Local Disk Persistence
components.role: persists subgraph output locally when the per-subgraph heuristic decides to do so

flows.what: groups the subgraph into Main/Regular/Merger by side-effect annotation (A1)
instruments inter-subgraph edges with Remote Pipes (A2)
decides whether to persist the subgraph's output locally (A3)

content.key_idea: FRACTAL compiles a shell script into a DFG, classifies subgraphs (Main/Regular/Merger), instruments edges with exactly-once Remote Pipes, then a Coordinator schedules and monitors replicated Executors that run subgraphs in a non-blocking event loop with optional local persistence.
content.reading_order: Left-to-right: shell script through PaSh-JIT into an annotated DFG (A1-3), into the Coordinator's scheduling/monitoring (A4-6), out to the replicated Executors' event loops (B1-4).

style.font: Times New Roman serif for labels (5.5-7.5pt) plus a monospace font for the embedded shell script

encoding.color_means: purple = Regular subgraphs, pale lavender = Main subgraphs, pink = Merger subgraphs (aggregator vertices like sort -m), matching the in-figure Main/Merger/Regular/Remote-Pipe legend; peach/orange = the Coordinator's monitoring and scheduling boxes; pale green = Executor internals
encoding.line_style_means: small blue circles mark Remote Pipe primitives inserted at inter-subgraph edges; a dashed line (B4) connects the two Executors as peers; solid arrows carry the compile-schedule-execute data flow
encoding.emphasis: letter-number tags (A1-A6, B1-B4) pin every part of the figure directly to the numbered explanation in the design section, and the color-coded Main/Merger/Regular legend lets the same DFG chain be read twice -- once as a plain shell pipeline, once annotated with FRACTAL's fault-tolerance machinery
reusable_patterns: a small color-swatch legend placed inline to key a pipe/DFG diagram
paired identical subsystem boxes (two Executors) with a dashed peer link to indicate replication
letter-number callouts (A1-6, B1-4) tying diagram regions directly to the prose
weaknesses: very high element count (258 shapes, 74 text boxes) in a wide double-column figure makes some labels (e.g., individual B-callouts) small and hard to read
the left DFG-compilation portion and the right Coordinator/Executor portion are visually different styles (pipe-chain vs. boxes) stitched into one figure

evidence: FRACTAL builds on PaSh-JIT to retrieve a DFG representation of the target script
groups subgraphs into one of three types with different fault-recovery semantics
Executors (Fig. 3, B1-4) receive their assigned subgraphs, reconstruct them into shell scripts

summary: Figure 3 shows FRACTAL's end-to-end architecture for fault-tolerant shell-script distribution. Starting from a client shell script, PaSh-JIT compiles it into a data-flow graph (blk1, blk2); the Coordinator then applies side-effect annotations to classify subgraphs as Main, Regular, or Merger (A1), instruments inter-subgraph edges with exactly-once Remote Pipe primitives (A2), and decides per-subgraph whether to persist outputs locally (A3) -- summarized in an inline Main/Merger/Regular/Remote-Pipe legend. The Coordinator's Progress Monitor, Scheduler, and Health Monitor (A4-6) then assign subgraphs to replicated Executors, shown as two peer boxes on the right; each Executor (B1-4) reconstructs its subgraph into a shell script and runs it via an Executor Runtime, Event Queue, and non-blocking Event loop, reading from a DFS File Reader and optionally writing to Local Disk Persistence. The figure is a dense, wide double-column diagram mixing pipe-chain glyphs, a small color legend, and boxed components tied together by letter-number callouts.
summary_zh: 该图展示FRACTAL架构：脚本经PaSh-JIT编译为DFG，协调器标注子图类型并插桩Remote Pipe（A1-3）；进度/调度/健康监控（A4-6）分配子图给多个执行器，执行器（B1-4）以事件循环运行并读写DFS与本地磁盘。
notes: layout-proposal: compile-coordinate-execute fan-out — a left-to-right chain from shell script through PaSh-JIT DFG annotation (A1-3) and the Coordinator's three monitors (A4-6) that then fans out to multiple peer Executors (B1-4); pipeline captures the left-to-right narrative but not the coordinator's hub-and-spoke fan-out to replicated executors.
